chunks: Ja'far b. al-Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ja'far b. Batta narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad b. Sinan, from 'Abdullah b. Muskan, from Abi 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:

Indeed, the most deserving of people to wish wealth for others are the miserly, because when people become rich they would stop seeking their money. And the most deserving of people to wish righteousness for others are those with flaws, because when people become righteous they would stop pursuing their flaws. And the most deserving of people to wish forbearance for others are the foolish who need to be pardoned for their foolishness.

Yet the miserly wish poverty upon the people, and those with flaws wish flaws upon the people, and the foolish wish foolishness upon the people. In poverty lies the need to turn to the miser, in corruption lies the exposure of the flawed, and in foolishness lies the recompense with sins.

key_terms.البخلاء: The miserly (al-bukhala') - those who withhold wealth despite having it
key_terms.الحلم: Forbearance (al-hilm) - patience and clemency in the face of provocation
key_terms.السفه: Foolishness (al-safah) - recklessness and lack of wisdom
key_terms.الصلاح: Righteousness or rectitude (al-salah) - moral and spiritual soundness
key_terms.المكافأة بالذنوب: Recompense with sins - mutual exchange of transgressions among the foolish

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the irony of human wishes regarding wealth, righteousness, and forbearance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches a profound paradox about human nature and self-interest. He explains that the miserly should logically wish for others to be wealthy (so no one asks them for money), the flawed should wish for others to be righteous (so no one scrutinizes their defects), and the foolish should wish for others to be forbearing (so they are pardoned). Yet ironically, each group does the opposite, which ultimately harms themselves.
